Chief Executive’s Foreword 
 
 I hope you enjoyed the summer break and got to enjoy all 
that Fingal has to offer. Our parks, beaches and harbours as 
well as our heritage properties are always popular choices 
for visitors looking to enjoy a day out and were particularly 
busy over the last couple of months. Maintaining our 
outdoor spaces and visitor attractions to excellent 
standards is something we take pride in and I was very 
pleased that Skerries and Portmarnock beaches were 
awarded the highest ranking in the latest IBAL (Irish 
Business Against Litter) Report. The report noted that 
Portmarnock deserved a ‘special mention’ for being 
“exceptionally freshly presented and maintained”. The IBAL 
inspectors said there are “excellent facilities for waste 
disposal and clearly marked recycling bins/clothing 
donation units”. Inspectors also made particular reference 
to the Skerries Beach Toy Library- Borrow, Play Return, 
describing it as a “lovely feature”, and the “excellent signage 
throughout” the area including St. Patrick's Way and Art 
Trail; Skerries Islands; Active Travel 'Cycling without Age, 
Skerries'; 'Safari in Skerries' and 'Adopt a Beach'”. The very 
positive report on Portmarnock Beach noted that it had 
made a “dramatic improvement”. IBAL inspectors said that 
“based on the very minimal litter observed over a long 
stretch of beach / car park area / pathway, it would seem 
that the council are very attentive at Portmarnock”. There 
was also praise for the availability of clean and well labelled 
litter bins as well as mention of the exceptional cleanliness 
of the walking paths leading to the beach noting their 
‘excellent condition’. I wish to extend my thanks to the 
Operations Department and the operational crews on the 
ground who work diligently to ensure these areas of natural 
beauty remain clean and safe for visitors Our collaborations 
with Tidy Towns groups and local volunteer groups have 
also been instrumental in achieving such good results and I 
also wish to extend my thanks to all involved.  
 
National Heritage Week took place from August 16th – 24th 
and was a truly enjoyable, educational and inspirational 
week for those who took part. This year’s theme ‘Exploring 
our Foundations’ invited us to celebrate the building blocks 
of our heritage from landscapes to buildings and traditional 
skills to stories. Celebrating Fingal’s archaeological, built 
natural and cultural heritage, a huge number of events took 
place across the county to promote awareness of our 
heritage, thereby encouraging its conservation and 
preservation. From architectural tours of Malahide Castle 
and Newbridge House and walks through the historical 
demesne of Kenure with Rush Tourism to braving the 
elements with the coastal Eire 6 Howth Walk & Talk, there 
was a varied and interesting programme which appealed to 
all ages and interests. Our native language is vibrant and 
alive when spoken and a wonderful evening of Ceol, Craic 
agus Gaeilge to celebrate our language was held in County 
Hall Swords on Monday August 18th.  
 
A podcast as Gaeilge was also produced featuring some 
Fingal 
staff 
and 
what 
Heritage 
means 
to 
them. 
Performances from the Fingal Mummers in Ballyboughal, 
Create your own Castle in Ardgillan Castle and genealogy 
workshops in Swords made up some of the 50 events which 
were well attended and really captured the essence of the 
week.   
 
I am very pleased that Fingal County Council has been 
shortlisted in several categories in this year’s Excellence in  
Local Government Awards. This year, Chambers Ireland 
received a record number of applications for these awards, 
with Fingal receiving nominations for the following: 
 
•  Howth Maritime & Seafood Festival (Festival of the Year) 
•  Promotion of Affordable Housing scheme       
   (Communications) 
•  Fingal Sports Festival (Health & Wellbeing) 
•  Sheltered Housing at Monastery Court, Lusk (Age Friendly  
    Initiative) 
•  Meakstown Community Centre and Bloom Community  
    Garden (Supporting Sustainable Communities) 
 
As with previous years, the calibre of submissions is 
extremely high and to be shortlisted in these categories is a 
testament to the ongoing work we carry out across a range 
of activities for the people of Fingal. The awards, which are 
sponsored 
by 
the 
Department 
of 
Housing, 
Local 
Government and Heritage, aim to acknowledge and 
celebrate the work being carried out by Local Authorities all 
over Ireland. On behalf of myself and the Executive 
Management Team, I wish to congratulate our teams who 
have demonstrated such commitment and diligence 
through their work on these projects and initiatives. The 
awards take place on Thursday, November 27th in the 
Crowne Plaza Hotel, Northwood and I know you will join 
with me in wishing our colleagues the very best of luck on 
the night. 
 
The best of the weather may be behind us but we still have 
some fantastic events to look forward to in the coming 
months in Fingal with the spectacular annual Fingal Festival 
of Fire on Halloween evening in locations across Fingal, 
Christmas Tree Lighting events, Christmas Markets and New 
Year’s Eve fireworks all ahead of us! I look forward to 
bringing you more information on these and other events 
next month. 
 
Best wishes, 
 
AnnMarie Farrelly 
Chief Executive

Smart Balbriggan 
In July, Smart Balbriggan hosted the CONNECT 
Centre Quantum & Answers Trailer from Trinity 
College, alongside the Smart Balbriggan Internet

Flavours of Fingal event.  These initiatives provided 
members 
of 
the 
public 
with 
interactive

technology, and the evolution of IoT through

Page 2 
 
 
On August 8th and 9th, Smart Balbriggan 
organised a two-day symposium focused on 
Artificial Intelligence, with sessions held in 
Balbriggan and at Trinity College Dublin. The event 
brought together scientists, academic researchers, 
and artists in collaboration with the SCÉAL 
Collective, funded by Research Ireland.  
 
The artists will now spend a couple months 
developing an art exhibition, workshops, music 
events and more to engage the community about 
science and technology.  
 
 
 
These will be part of the annual "How It’s Made" 
festival, now in its third year, which will take place 
from November 13–15, 2025, under the theme 
"Unmasking AI" and is funded by Science Week 
(Research Ireland).

Digital Statistics 
The fingal.ie website had 280,083 visitors during 
July and August which was an increase of 110,000 
from June. The number of page views rose by 
255,100 to 618,581 while the average time spent 
on the site reduced by three seconds to 1 minute 
and 58 seconds.  
 
Figures for the first eight months of the year are 
down on the same period in 2024. There have been

The most popular pages during July and August

There were 61,748 impressions and 901 reactions

278,180 impressions.  
 
The WhatsApp channel now has 3,369 followers

(1,076) and Bluesky (446).

Malahide Castle and Gardens

have received the 2025 Tripadvisor Travellers’

visitor attractions worldwide. 
 
What makes this recognition especially meaningful 
is that it is driven entirely by positive visitor reviews 
and ratings from the past year. It is a genuine 
reflection of the memorable experiences that 
visitors have had at these two much-loved 
attractions.

experiences. Thanks to the fantastic feedback from

Casino Model Railway Museum 
A new experience in Fingal’s event offering, the 
Malahide Food Market launched this summer in 
the scenic grounds of the Casino Model Railway 
Museum, conveniently located beside Malahide 
DART station. Organised by Fingal County Council 
in collaboration with the Fingal Food Circle and 
Fingal Farmers Group, the market is running on the 
fourth Saturday of each month from July to 
September.

The market showcases a selection of artisan foods, 
organic local produce, and handcrafted goods 
from talented Fingal based producers and makers. 
It provides a welcoming, community focused 
atmosphere for families and food lovers alike. 
 
Free entry to both the market and the Casino 
Model Railway Museum is offered during market 
hours, making it an accessible and enjoyable day 
out for all. 
 
This initiative highlights Fingal’s ongoing support 
for local food, farming, and craft communities, 
while enriching the cultural and tourism offering in 
Malahide.

Department of Transport originally communicated

set for these.   This was changed  as there is no 
definition of urban areas in legislation with regards 
to the setting of speed limits.  In order to 
implement a default 30kph in urban areas, there 
would need to be updated legislation which would 
take some time. 
 
Therefore 
the 
Department 
of 
Transport 
communicated to Councils that we were to 
proceed with the review and implementation of 
urban speed limits by special speed limit bye-laws 
rather than a change in the default speed limit.  In 
order to undertake the process of setting special 
speed limits in built up & urban areas, the 
Guidelines for Setting and Managing Speed Limits 
in Ireland are being revised.  They have not yet 
been issued to us.  The best timeframe we have is 
that they will be issued in Q3 2025 via a new 
Circular.  The circular will direct the LA’s to 
commence the process of reviewing speed limits in 
our areas and to set speed limits in accordance 
with the new Guidelines. We attended a workshop 
where feedback was taken on board from Traffic 
Engineers to assist with the finalising of revisions 
to the Guidelines which we are still waiting for. 
 
The Council have not received any further 
information from the Department of Transport.

Preventing Homelessness, Notices to Quit and

Fingal County Council is aware that households in 
the Fingal area who may have received a notice to 
quit, which is also referred to as a notice of 
termination, from their landlord may be worried or 
unsure of what to do.  Fingal County Council and 
the Dublin Regional Homeless Executive (DRHE) 
would like to advise anyone affected of the services 
that are available to them in these circumstances.  
 
We strongly encourage tenants residing in the 
Fingal area, who have been issued with a notice 
of termination, to contact Fingal County 
Council as soon as they receive a notice from 
their landlord. The contact details for Fingal 
County Council are provided at the bottom of 
this page.  
 
When the tenants contact Fingal County Council, staff 
in the Housing Department will take note of the 
termination date.  
 
The Council advises the tenant to refer the notice to 
Threshold, a service funded by the DRHE to provide a 
Tenancy Protection Service for private renters in the 
Dublin Region, including Fingal. Threshold can also be 
contacted directly on Freephone 1800 454 454 or via 
their website www.threshold.ie which contains more 
information and advice on the validity of your notice.  
 
The Council’s first response will be to try to prevent 
homelessness. This includes assessing the person’s 
position on the social housing list, providing advice on 
applying for Choice Based Lettings, and advising the 
person on the level of Housing Assistance Payment 
(HAP) they may be eligible to receive. 
  
Placement in emergency accommodation will be a 
last resort if no other alternative can be identified.

Fingal County Council continues to liaise with other 
Dublin and neighboring local authorities to deal 
with tenancy issues that may require an inter-
authority approach.  In particular, we are working 
closely with our colleagues in the other Dublin 
Local Authorities on the implementation of the 
Government policy and guidance, with a focus on 
the needs of tenants.   
  
Whilst the Council will, in the context of current 
circumstances, adopt flexibility in dealing with 
potential acquisitions of properties with tenants in 
situ, any acquisition is subject to appropriate due 
diligence and checks before any commitment is 
made 
to 
acquire, 
including, 
for 
example, 
determining that a valid notice of termination is in 
place, the tenant has a social housing need, and 
the condition and valuation of the property.  
  
The Government has put forward options to allow 
tenants who are not eligible for social housing to 
remain in their homes, including schemes to 
support the purchase of homes and a Cost Rental 
in-situ Scheme. The Cost Rental Tenant-in-Situ 
Scheme is available for tenants who are not eligible 
for social housing and are at risk of homelessness. 
The DHLGH has advised that local authorities are 
to be the first point of contact for this scheme, but 
it is managed by the Housing Agency. Under the 
scheme, the Housing Agency can purchase a

Council will undertake an initial assessment of the 
tenant’s circumstances and refer details to the 
Housing Agency for consideration, where the 
tenant is at risk of homelessness and the Cost 
Rental Tenant-in-Situ scheme applies. The Housing 
Agency will then contact the landlord about the 
purchase of the property.
